title: [Chapitre] IX et IX bis. [Ateliers] : notes manuscrites (05-15/07/1986).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting, from pp. 78–80. A 'dispositif' is a set E with a binary relation x |o| y, which reads as orthogonality or disjointness. For A ⊆ E, ∁A (Comp°) is the set of points orthogonal to every point of A. Σ_E is the set of closed subsets, those with A = ∁∁A. Σ_E is a complete lattice with an order-reversing complement ∁ satisfying ∁∁ = id, and σ_E sends x to its closure. Σ_E is the lattice of biorthogonally closed sets of the polarity defined by |o|. An abstract 'système' Σ is a complete lattice with such a complement.

The theorem in progress (stated on p. 78) gives a converse. Suppose Σ is a système and σ: E → Σ satisfies:
(a) x |o| y iff σ(x) ≤ ∁σ(y);
(b) σ(E) is join-dense, i.e. every S equals the sup of the σ(x) lying below it.
Then there is a unique isomorphism α: Σ_E → Σ compatible with complements, given by α(A) = sup_{x∈A} σ(x).

Previous page. With β(S) = {x : σ(x) ≤ S}, it is shown that β(S) lies in Σ_E and that β(∁S) = ∁β(S).

This page.
1. β: Σ → Σ_E is monotone, and αβ = id_Σ by density (b). β is compatible with complements (C).
2. It remains to show βα = id_{Σ_E}. Then α and β are mutually inverse order-isomorphisms, and compatibility with ∁ transfers from β.
3. Take A ∈ Σ_E and A' = ∁A. For x ∈ A and x' ∈ A', σ(x) and σ(x') are orthogonal by (a). Hence the sups α(A) and α(A') are orthogonal, i.e. α(A) ≤ ∁α(A').
4. Applying the monotone, complement-compatible β gives βα(A) ≤ β∁α(A') = ∁βα(A'), i.e. βα(A) |o| βα(A').
5. Trivially A ⊆ βα(A) and A' ⊆ βα(A'). The Lemma then gives A = βα(A) and A' = βα(A').
6. Lemma: in a système, if A ≤ B, A' ≤ B', B |o| B' (i.e. B ≤ ∁B') and A' = ∁A, then A = B and A' = B'. Proof: A ≤ B ≤ ∁B' ≤ ∁A' = A, so all inequalities are equalities.

The next page settles uniqueness of α via join-density in Σ_E. It then begins a corollary on dense subsets E' ⊆ E inducing Σ_E ≅ Σ_{E'}.

In modern terms, this is the representation of a complete ortholattice (or a complete lattice with an involutive antitone complement) as the lattice of biorthogonally closed subsets of an orthogonality space via a join-dense generating set. It is an analogue of the universal characterisation of the Dedekind–MacNeille completion / Galois-connection closure systems.
errors: No genuine error. Steps 1–6 are correct given the setup: ∁ antitone and involutive on Σ, sups in Σ preserving orthogonality to a fixed element (which follows from ∁ being antitone), and condition (a).
Minor gap: the Lemma's last equality ∁A' = A uses that A is closed (∁∁A = A). This holds since A ∈ Σ_E, or holds in the abstract système, but it is not said explicitly.
Minor gap: 'α(A), α(A') le sont aussi' (sups of pairwise orthogonal families are orthogonal) is left implicit. It follows from S ≤ ∁T iff T ≤ ∁S and the definition of sup.

ideas.what: Lattice of biorthogonally closed subsets of a set with an orthogonality relation (Σ_E with complement ∁)
ideas.modern_name: Orthogonality space / polarity closure lattice; ortholattice of orthoclosed sets
ideas.usually_credited_to: Birkhoff (polarities, 1940); Dacey (1968), Foulis–Randall (orthogonality spaces, quantum logic)

ideas.what: Characterisation of Σ_E up to unique isomorphism by an order-embedding condition (a) plus join-density (b)
ideas.modern_name: Representation of complete ortholattices via join-dense orthogonality spaces; analogue of the Dedekind–MacNeille completion's universal property
ideas.usually_credited_to: MacLaren (1964), Dacey (1968); Banaschewski / Schmidt for MacNeille-type characterisations

ideas.what: Lemma: A ≤ B, A' ≤ B', B ⊥ B', A' = ∁A imply A = B and A' = B'
ideas.modern_name: Maximality of complementary pairs in an orthocomplemented lattice

missed.claim: Grothendieck in July 1986 independently develops the theory of orthogonality spaces and their complete ortholattices of closed sets (the 'dispositifs' and 'systèmes' of the 'Ateliers' chapters), including a representation theorem. This is standard in quantum-logic and lattice-theory literature, but its presence in his late notes is a historical fact not reflected in the record.
missed.quote: car alors α et β sont des iso. d'ensembles ordonnés l'une de l'autre, et (comme on voit sur β) compatibles : C.
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Historical interest only: it documents the topics of Grothendieck's 1986 foundational work. The mathematics itself is known.

deep.surprise_reason: A clean but routine proof of a known representation theorem for lattices of orthoclosed sets. Nothing mathematically new. It is mildly interesting that Grothendieck was working on this in 1986.
transcription_corrections: 'sont des points dans Cours [?] Supp [?]' most likely reads 'sont des points deux à deux orthog[onaux]' (pairwise orthogonal), and 'la sont aussi' should be 'le sont aussi'.
The crossed-out symbol before β in '[-α-]β = id_Σ' is a scribbled α; the intended statement is αβ = id_Σ.
'A' = ∁A^E' is ∁A, possibly with the superscript indicating the complement taken in E (Comp°).
'Lemme Soit Σ un système (Σ_E ou l'ensemble [?])' plausibly reads '(Σ_E ou l'abstrait)' or similar; uncertain.
